With tiny learning rates the network is undertrained after 243 epochs, so increasing the rate helps a lot (exps 9-10).
Lowering an already-small learning rate pushes further into undertraining (exps 18-19).
Once the L2 penalty is large, increasing it further causes heavy underfitting (exps 81-86), whereas at small alpha the change is negligible.
Relaxing an overly strong L2 penalty restores model capacity and yields big gains (exps 93-96).
Deeper ReLU nets are less stable at high learning rates, so adding a layer there is harmful (exps 43-44).
At low learning rates extra depth adds representational power and speeds fitting without instability (exps 41, 45).
Smaller batches give more update steps, compensating for a too-small learning rate (exps 27, 37).
Wider layers fit faster under slow learning rates, so widening helps more in that regime (exps 61, 69, 78).

- **Learning rate:** stepping it up hurts near the unstable top of its range and helps when training is too slow at the bottom. Stepping it down does the reverse.
- **Penalty strength (alpha):** at the high end it dominates. Raising it further is strongly harmful, and lowering it is strongly helpful.
- **Depth and batch size:** both interact with the learning-rate regime. Extra depth helps at low learning rates but destabilizes at high ones. Smaller batches compensate for low learning rates through more updates.
- **Width:** extra width helps more when the learning rate is low.
